title: Audio Video and Video Conferencing Solutions
subject: AUDIO VIDEO
description: Components of a meeting room, room types, acoustics, network requirements, and how to run a site survey for a video conferencing setup.

lessons.title: Components of a video conferencing system
lessons.body:
A video conferencing room needs these parts to work together:

- **Camera:** captures the room. Framing and zoom matter more than resolution alone.
- **Microphones:** capture speech from every seat. Ceiling or table arrays suit most rooms.
- **Speakers:** play remote audio clearly, usually with echo cancellation.
- **Display:** shows remote participants and shared content.
- **Codec or conferencing unit:** encodes and decodes the call, and connects to the network or cloud service.
- **Control:** a touch panel or remote to start calls and manage devices.

A weak microphone or poor acoustics damages a call more than a low-resolution camera.

lessons.title: Room types and acoustics
lessons.body:
Rooms are usually grouped by size and purpose:

- **Huddle room:** two to four people, a single screen and a small camera.
- **Medium room:** six to ten people, with ceiling or table microphones.
- **Boardroom:** larger groups, with multiple cameras and a stronger audio design.

Acoustics affect clarity. Hard surfaces, such as glass walls and bare floors, create echo. Soft furnishings, ceiling tiles, and correct microphone placement reduce it. Recommend acoustic treatment when a room has hard surfaces.

lessons.title: Network and power requirements
lessons.body:
Video calls need reliable bandwidth in both directions. Bandwidth per call depends on the resolution and the number of participants, and the vendor's sizing guide should be used for each design. Plan for:

- Enough upload and download capacity at the site, with headroom for other users.
- Quality of service (QoS) settings that prioritise real-time traffic.
- Power outlets and cabling for each device, with a UPS for the conferencing system where outages would disrupt key meetings.

Confirm these requirements before quoting, not after installation.

lessons.title: Running a site survey
lessons.body:
A site survey captures the facts needed for a correct design:

- Room dimensions, seating layout, and where the screen and camera will sit.
- Existing wall, ceiling, and cabling routes.
- Lighting, windows, and noise sources.
- Network points and available bandwidth.
- Users' typical meeting size and the platform they use.

Use the survey to write a design that the customer can approve. Changes found during installation cost more than changes found during the survey.
